prompt: wget time-stamping Content-Length size mismatch behavior
answer:
With `wget -N`/`--timestamping`, Wget compares the local and remote timestamps and sizes. The documented behavior is:

- If the local file does not exist, Wget downloads it.
- If the local and remote sizes differ, Wget downloads the remote file regardless of timestamps.
- Otherwise, Wget downloads only when the remote file is newer.
- For HTTP, Wget checks `Last-Modified` and also compares the `Content-Length` header as an additional size check.  
  Sources: [Time-Stamping](https://www.gnu.org/software/wget/manual/html_node/Time_002dStamping.html), [HTTP Time-Stamping Internals](https://www.gnu.org/software/wget/manual/html_node/HTTP-Time_002dStamping-Internals.html)

However, the search results document an exception/bug involving resuming with `-c`: if Wget sends `If-Modified-Since` and the server responds `304 Not Modified`, Wget may omit the download without detecting that the local file has a different size. Without `If-Modified-Since`, a too-large local file can produce HTTP `416 Range Not Satisfiable`, which the reported Wget behavior also treated as “not modified” rather than redownloading.

For bogus server `Content-Length` headers, use `--ignore-length`; this makes Wget ignore that header.
